unresolved_questions: The calling convention is an inference, not a record. The machine-derived ABI record abstains outright (verdict ABI_UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN) because the body has no terminal RET, and the live decompilation carries 'WARNING: Unknown calling convention'. thiscall is the best-supported reading -- the tail target's own RET 0x4 pops the one forwarded word, and the receiver travels in ECX -- and it is what the model declares, but nothing in the target's own two instructions proves it. This is the sole reason the ABI check is a WARN rather than a PASS, and no source change can move it.

Is the receiver a UTFWin::GlideEffect IBiStateEffect subobject, or the same-offset subobject of a sibling effect class? The SDK places IBiStateEffect at +0x0c and the adjustment is 0x0C, but the byte-for-byte identical shape at 0x0097e550 (UTFWin::InflateEffect::func88h) and the -0x04 shape at 0x0096ff80 make the two-instruction form non-distinguishing, and the static image does not settle it. The model therefore names no class at all.

Which vftable, if any, places 0x0096ff70 in a destructor slot? Ghidra's vtable detection never ran on this program, so the only evidence is a DATA pointer at +0x08 of a run based at 0x01442584 whose length exceeds any single vftable, while the SDK's func88h naming convention implies offset 0x88 (whose slot in that run holds 0x00951220, UTFWin::GetAllocator). The destructor reading stays a hypothesis and is not used.

Why does the SDK declare three int parameters when the machine forwards one stack word? The extra words may be unused register-class artefacts of the SDK method-header generator. The model declares the one word the machine shows.

Who calls this, and with what deleting flag? There is no code caller; the only reference is the DATA pointer at 0x0144258c. Nothing in the static image establishes the values the word takes in real use.

Is the -0x0C receiver the subobject the vptr was reached through, or an unrelated pointer the caller happened to hold? Deciding it needs a runtime trace of the value in ECX at 0x0096ff70, which this repository has never run.

conditions: The original process is driven to a point where the pointer run at 0x01442584 is dispatched through, so the value in ECX at 0x0096ff70 is observed.

The word left in EAX at the RET 0x4 is recorded and compared against the reconstructed void signature.

expected_reasons.ABI: WARN, and not fixable from this package. The check reaches its confidence arm because the machine-derived record carries conventions.confidence UNKNOWN: the derivation abstained (verdict ABI_UNKNOWN, abstained_because 'no_terminal_ret: the only exit observed is a tail jump'), so the oracle is not proven. The two arms above it cannot be reached either: there is no unresolved ABI conflict (both conflicts lists are empty), and the source convention does not contradict a claimed one -- the persisted record's 'thiscall adjustor thunk with one forwarded stack word' resolves to thiscall and the source declares thiscall, so the FAIL arm for a contradiction does not fire. Declaring no convention at all would make this worse, not better: the last arm is also a WARN.
expected_reasons.CALLS: PASS. The xref export's single out-edge (0x0096ff73 -> 0x0096ffd0, direct-call) and the complete two-instruction listing's single direct transfer name the same set, and the source span names exactly that one target and no other, through the address-suffixed callee symbol dfw_tail_deleting_0096ffd0. Note that the validator reads JMP as a transfer as well as CALL, which is what lets a tail-call body pass this check at all.
expected_reasons.GLOBALS: PASS by evidenced absence. The complete listing names no data-segment address and the source span names none either. There is no second machine side to corroborate against (data_reference_count is 0 and the export carries no data-reference edge type), and for an absence none is needed.
expected_reasons.FIELDS/OFFSETS: PASS on the receiver-agnostic absence arm. The machine-derived receiver record names no register, so nothing is claimed about the receiver in either direction; separately the listing was consumed in full by the machine parse (2 of 2, unparsed 0) and contains no memory operand through any register, which is the evidence that the body performs no field access, and the source span declares no field offset either. The model deliberately keeps the -0x0C adjustment out of the function's own text (it is a named constant, and the header's static assertion ties it to the jump displacement), so no displacement is declared that would have to be grounded.
expected_reasons.CONSTANTS: PASS. The source span states no hexadecimal literal, so there is none the fully parsed listing could lack (2 of 2 instructions, 0 unparsed). This was a design constraint, not luck: the span text carries no 0x token at all. Writing the adjustment inline as 0x0c would also have passed, but only because the listing spells it 0xc and the check compares token strings -- 0x0c and 0xc are different tokens, so the literal spelling the listing uses is the one that would have been required.
expected_reasons.CONTROL FLOW: PASS. The complete listing has no conditional branch, which is itself the evidence that the body is straight-line. The source span declares no branch keyword either; keyword shape is not part of this verdict either way.
expected_reasons.VIRTUAL DISPATCH: PASS. No indirect transfer through a register or a memory operand in the body, and the machine dispatch record agrees at 0. The source span declares no slot boundary -- it names no identifier containing vtable, load_slot, object_slot, shell_slot or slot[ -- so there is no slot claim to refute.
expected_reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS: PASS, partial coverage. The bounded ABI record's return_type is void and the reconstructed declaration is void, so they agree. The check is satisfied on the type name alone: it does not and cannot see the separate question of what the tail target leaves in EAX.

limits: A branch invented in this frame whose two arms are indistinguishable is not caught, because no behavioural test can distinguish it: the mutation `if (flag & 1) call(); else call();` still passes. Only a branch that changes an observable (M4) is caught. This is a property of behavioural testing, not a gap in the assertions, and it is stated rather than papered over.

A store that wrote back the value it had just read would leave the receiver's bytes identical and would pass the memcmp. Nothing in the two instructions can produce one, and the check does not claim to exclude it; every store that changes a byte is excluded (M6).

A read of the receiver that changed no byte would not be observed either. The listing contains no memory operand, so no reconstruction that follows it reads anything; a hypothetical one that did would be unobservable through this interface.

The stack-neutrality check writes its call site out in inline assembly, so it verifies the callee-cleaned stack effect and not the compiler's choice of argument passing. It cannot distinguish a thiscall from a stdcall -- the two agree on x86-32 -- and it is not available on a compiler without GNU-style inline asm, where it reports that it could not be measured instead of passing quietly.

portability_notes: Built and run clean with g++ 16.2.1 and clang++ 22.1.8 at -O0, -O1, -O2, -O3, -Os and -Og, with and without -DNDEBUG, and with -fPIC, -no-pie and -static. The generated body was inspected at -O2: it emits `sub $0xc,%ecx` and ends in `ret $0x4`, which is the machine's SUB ECX,0x0C and the frame's RET 0x4.

clang++ -m32 -O2 -fno-pic links a PIE with a DT_TEXTREL text relocation and then crashes on the first PLT call into libc. A three-line program with no code from this package reproduces the same linker warnings under the same flags, and the same program passes with -no-pie, so this is a toolchain/linker interaction with that flag combination and not a defect in this package. Every default configuration passes.

tooling_observations: A metadata sidecar's `observed_mechanics` list is never projected into the index record: tools/reconstruction_knowledge.py reads that field only from the manifest's function records (line 951), and extract_metadata collects just unresolved_questions, blockers, runtime_gates, source_files, source_provenance and evidence from a sidecar. The CONSTANTS check falls back to that transcript only when no listing exists (tools/reconstruction_tooling/validate.py, CONSTANTS arm), so a worker's transcript can never reach it through a sidecar.

The ABI check's 'the derived ABI record abstained (ABI_UNKNOWN)' arm is unreachable for any current pack. It reads the verdict from the envelope returned by _abi_category, which inspects categories['abi'] only; the derived record -- and its verdict: ABI_UNKNOWN -- lives in categories['abi_derived']. Every pack that keeps the two apart therefore falls through to the confidence arm. For this target the observable effect is the wording of the WARN ('derived calling-convention confidence is UNKNOWN' rather than 'the derived ABI record abstained'), not the status, so nothing is mis-graded; it is reported because the arm looks like it should be reachable and is not.

Index collision to know about before integrating: extract_metadata merges every sidecar that claims a VA, and validate._source takes the first existing candidate in that merged, sorted list. reconstruction/staging/pkg-dfw-0096ff70 sorts before reconstruction/staging/pkg-utfwin-glideeffect-func88h, so once this sidecar is present the judged source for 0x0096ff70 becomes this package's .cpp. That is the intent, and it is also a side effect on another package's package, so the integrator should know it happens.
